The bug causes an incorrect gradient norm computation by using param.grad instead of decoupled_grad, so a runtime check for gradient-norm-computation-fidelity would detect the violation.
The bug causes only one checkpoint file to be written instead of one per TP rank, violating checkpoint-save-completeness (T12) which requires that the set of files covers all expected TP ranks.
The bug is a source-level scheduler intent mismatch that cannot be detected from runtime traces because both schedulers produce plausible monotonic lr curves.
The bug causes a mismatch between the saved and loaded expert parameter fragment per rank, violating checkpoint-restore-state-equality.
The bug is a source-level operand error in a lerp call that changes the target of the lerp, which is not exposed by any standard runtime trace field, so no taxonomy invariant can detect it.
The bug causes a mismatch in optimizer param_groups after loading a checkpoint, which would violate a runtime invariant that checks checkpoint-restore-state-equality.
The bug causes a specific sigmoid operation to receive bf16 input instead of fp32, which would violate a designated-dtype-fidelity invariant checking the expected dtype of that op.

The bug causes the gradient norm to be underestimated due to missing accumulation, directly violating gradient-norm-computation-fidelity.

The bug causes the user-supplied configuration value to be ignored due to a misspelled key; a runtime check comparing user-supplied value to engine-parsed value would fail, which is exactly what T18 (configured-value-effectiveness) is designed to detect.

The bug causes a tensor's dtype to be int instead of float, which directly violates the 'designated-dtype-fidelity' invariant that checks if a tensor's runtime dtype matches its expected designated type.
The bug causes a detached tensor (requires_grad=False) to be included in the loss, violating the invariant that the loss is properly gradient-connected to parameters.

The bug fails to reset self.global_step when cfg.restore_dataloader is False, so a runtime invariant checking that after restore, global_step is properly reset (dataloader bookkeeping reset) would be violated.

The bug causes the TopKRouter module to lack the calculate_per_token_loss attribute despite the config setting being True; a runtime check that configured values take effect would detect this missing attribute.
The bug is non-deterministic and source-only, so no runtime invariant check on trace fields can reliably detect the sporadic NaN partitions.
The bug requires inspecting per-worker index sets across workers, which is not captured by any runtime trace field in the given taxonomy, and thus no invariant can detect it at runtime.

The bug is not detectable via any runtime trace invariant because it requires a reference run and no trace field distinguishes it.

The bug cannot be reliably detected by any runtime invariant because the output indices may be identical and the gate values may accidentally satisfy range constraints; only source code analysis reveals the error.

The bug causes stale state to be captured in checkpoint because callbacks for completed futures haven't run yet, violating checkpoint-save-completeness.

The bug causes the learning rate trajectory to deviate from the reference sqrt-decay schedule, which would be detected by a specification reference conformance invariant comparing actual LR values to expected ones at each step.
The bug is a name-value mismatch in an enum that requires a semantic check on the string content, which is not covered by any taxonomy invariant; it would require a custom assertion.
The bug causes a mismatch between the cached self.dtype and the actual live weight dtype, which a designated-dtype-fidelity invariant checking input_dtype vs weight_dtype would catch.
The bug violates the config-invariant-execution-equivalence invariant because it includes init=False fields in the encoded dict, breaking the fixed-point encode-decode property.

Checking config-invariant-execution-equivalence would detect the discrepancy between fused and non-fused loss outputs when softmax_aux=True and fused=True, because the fused path hardcodes lse_square_scale=0 causing a different z_loss.
The bug causes uint16 token dtype to be used for uint32 data, violating storage-dtype-interpretation match.

The bug causes the gradient norm metric to be scaled by the number of replicas, which would be detected by comparing the logged metric to a reference single-replica run, i.e., spec-reference-conformance.
T16 checks positional encoding position fidelity; the bug fails to pass cu_doc_lens to RoPE, causing incorrect global positions for packed docs, which would violate this invariant.

The bug is only detectable by reading source code; no runtime trace field reliably distinguishes the buggy 'and' semantics from correct '&' semantics, so none of the invariant types would be violated.

The bug causes the main embedding to not receive the teacher-scaled initialization, so a runtime check of init-distribution-conformance would detect that param_mean/param_std deviate from expected teacher_stats.
The bug causes F.silu to be called with an extra argument, violating the expected call signature, which a spec-reference-conformance check on call_arg_count would detect.
The bug causes the tokens_processed counter to be incremented twice per batch instead of once, violating the exactly-once-side-effect invariant.

The bug causes a parameter to be initialized with the wrong variable, so a runtime invariant checking that actual parameter values conform to a reference specification (spec-reference-conformance) would detect the mismatch via checksum comparison.

Cross-rank equality of grad_norm across PP ranks would be violated because the bug prevents all-reducing grad_norm, causing each rank to have a different local norm instead of a consistent global norm.
The bug causes q/k/v tensors to have dtype bf16 instead of the expected fp32, which violates a designated-dtype-fidelity invariant on the input_dtype field.
The bug causes sort keys to wrap from uint32 underflow, violating sort-key order conformance which checks for proper ordering of keys in packing operations.
The bug omits a required call to _finalize_loss for hnet_embed_loss, violating the exactly-once side-effect requirement that every active loss component must have _finalize_loss called once.

The bug causes the 'freeze_experts' configuration option to be dropped after OmegaConf merge, so a runtime invariant checking that every configured value is actually present and effective (T18) would be violated because the intended value is missing from the final config.
T19 checks that packed sequences have proper attention isolation; the bug causes cross-attention because cu_doc_lens is not passed to the kernel, violating isolation.
The bug causes per-parameter all_reduce_call_count to differ from the expected count of 1, violating the exactly-once side-effect invariant.

The bug causes a logged metric value type to be DTensor instead of Tensor, which would violate an invariant ensuring logged metric reduction consistency (e.g., that metrics are of correct type for reduction).
Checking configured-value-effectiveness would compare the externally injected head_dim with the internally derived head_dim, and a mismatch would violate the invariant.
The bug causes `linear_proj.save_original_input` to be incorrectly true when `config.fp4` is true, violating a config-invariant execution equivalence that should hold.
The bug computes true_ratio using boundary_mask instead of byte_mask, including padding in the loss, which violates the padding-loss-exclusion invariant.

The bug causes a mismatch between the configured sliding window size and the actual window size argument passed to the attention kernel, which would violate the invariant that configured values are effectively applied.

The bug causes attention normalization to be applied to the wrong tensor (QKV projection output instead of attention output), violating the expected specification, so a spec-reference-conformance invariant would detect it.
The bug causes an incorrect loss division factor that would violate a scale-factor-consistency invariant comparing the actual loss_div_factor to the expected value derived from byte_positions shape.
The bug causes an expert label index to be out of valid range (3 vs 3 experts 0-2), which violates the supervision-label-index-range-validity invariant that checks index < num_experts.
The bug causes the loss value to become NaN, violating the invariant that scaling scalars (including loss) must be finite.
No taxonomy entry checks for finite values on intermediate tensors like y_space_hat_all; the bug's underflow to -inf would not be detected by any listed runtime invariant.
The bug silently changes the dtype of soft_target_probs from float to int, violating the designated-dtype-fidelity invariant (T05) which checks that tensor dtypes match expectations.
The bug causes multiple ranks to write to the same tmp file, violating the exactly-once side-effect invariant by creating duplicate file write targets.
The bug causes boundary positions to miss the required label offset, violating an exactly-once side effect invariant that each boundary position's offset must be applied before the loss computation.
The bug causes padded positions to affect label offsets, violating the padding-loss-exclusion invariant that ensures padding does not contribute to loss computation.
The bug violates a config precondition that at most one layer has source_group_size set, which a runtime check of config-invariant-execution-equivalence would detect by examining the trace fields.
The bug causes the config field `use_head_qk_norm` to be False instead of the expected True, which would violate a config-invariant-execution-equivalence check that validates this config value.

The bug causes MLA-specific projection parameters to be initialized to zero (or not initialized at all), and a runtime check of T27 (init-distribution-conformance) would detect this because the expected distribution (e.g., normal with nonzero std) would be violated.
The bug causes fingerprint_fields to miss layout-affecting attributes, which would violate a checkpoint-save-completeness invariant that checks that all such attributes are included.
T34 checks training-step-budget-data-sufficiency, and the bug causes sum(instances_per_path) to be less than training_steps * batch_size, violating this invariant.
The bug prevents proper initialization of the w_g parameter, and T27 checks that actual initialization distributions conform to expected ones, so a runtime check would detect the deviation.
The bug zeroes expert/router gradients unconditionally, so a runtime check for parameter-update-effectiveness (T22) would detect that non-frozen parameters have zero updates, violating the invariant.
T02 checks logged metric reduction consistency, which would detect that batch_metric_value is not divided by num_micro_batches.

The bug causes a mismatch between the configured window_size and the actual window size argument passed to flash-attn, which a check of configured-value-effectiveness (T18) on the runtime trace would detect.

The bug detaches ce_loss and z_loss from the computation graph, preventing gradients from flowing from these loss components to parameters, which violates the loss-parameter-gradient-connectivity invariant.

The bug causes an incorrect per-token loss due to a flawed allreduce of the loss divisor, which would be detected by a runtime check for logged-metric-reduction-consistency that verifies the consistency of the reduced loss metric across distributed ranks.
The bug fails to divide the accumulated loss by num_micro_batches, violating gradient accumulation conservation.
